findings.detail: The citation is dragonRider.ts lines 4-20 and supports only the core running/boss union. The claim also states that the component gamePhase union is start/playing/ended, which exists in DragonRiderGame.tsx lines 390-392 but is absent from the declared envelope.

The cited DragonRiderGame.tsx lines 153-165 contain stage and animation constants only. They do not contain the asserted 28/72-percent gates, 50/78-percent player, 50/28-percent boss placements, or the no-world-bounds/no-camera conclusion; those positions occur in a different uncited range.

The cited DragonRiderGame.tsx lines 124-150 declare asset URL constants. They do not establish the claim's separate proposition that those assets are loaded. A loading envelope is required for that atom or the wording must remain declaration-only.

The cited dragonRider.test.ts lines 19-91 support the core test summary only. The same claim also asserts component-test coverage of start/running status, keyboard selection, and boss-to-results behavior without citing DragonRiderGame.test.tsx.

The declared envelope covers only advanceToNextLevel. Its interpretation additionally states that a victory handled by the component leads to that reset state, but the component invocation at DungeonLiberatorGame.tsx lines 210-218 is not in the claim's citation.

The package labels history unknown even though the accepted T2 historical denominator already enumerates the deleted legacy page/test/API/component records and seven withdrawn dragon-rider cartridge files. It also does not reconcile the accepted cover, gameplay, duplicate asset-root, vocabulary, and physical asset candidates. This fails the required identity/route/implementation/copy/test/asset/history reconciliation.

The package omits the accepted simultaneous current-page/catalog-withdrawn identity state, page and component tests, sentence/ranking/completion API records and copy, and the accepted cover plus duplicate legacy/current asset-root candidates. One route claim and one source-path asset claim do not reconcile those denominator items.

All three requirements maps resolve their chosen IDs, but none supplies the protocol-required complete scene/state/transition model, mechanic-and-learning blueprint, and developer-effort decomposition. Dragon Rider also omits boss/result transition atoms, and Dungeon Liberator omits start/end and result-flow atoms that are present in reachable source.

The frozen strategy requires every actual budget unit to be an integer and says an unmeasured role is ineligible. Spellweaver collector and mapper elapsed_minutes are null; its active collector report itself records unmeasured_roles=1 and STOP-NON-AUTHORITATIVE. Dragon Rider and Dungeon Liberator browser receipts record unavailable source_bytes/source_files_objects/elapsed_minutes, and the Spellweaver browser receipt has null elapsed_minutes. The global provenance direction permits unavailable provider attestations, not missing local budget actuals, while the Spellweaver exception changes source_bytes only and expressly waives no other gate.

The V2 suite proves envelope hashes, metadata presence, ID resolution, selected bindings, and bounded browser dispositions, but it does not compare atomic claim meaning to the cited text, reconcile the accepted per-game denominator, require the mandated blueprint/effort outputs, or enforce all seven integer budget units for every selected role. It therefore reports these gates green while the nine High defects above remain mechanically invisible.
